To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have shown that the motive of HPn (as defined by Panin and Walter) splits in MWmotives, that we have extended this result to arbitrary symplectic bundles, and that we have given the Gysin triangles in MW-motives.
the motive of HPn splits in the category MotMWeff of effective MW-momotives, and that the Gysin sequence for a symplectic bundle is a triangle in the category MotW.
the motive of a quaternionic Grassmann bundle splits in the category MW of effective MW-moments, and that the Gysin sequence in MW-motives holds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the category of MW-motives, which is the category of motives defined by Déglise and Fasel.
the study of the category of effective motivic sheaves on a field k, denoted $$MW_k$$ M W k, introduced by Calmès–Déglise–Fasel.
the study of the category of MW-motives and the construction of its motivic cohomology theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results give a full picture of the theory of MW-motives in the case of the quaternionic projective spaces and their bundles.
the category of MW-motives is a good category to study the algebraic topology of symplectic manifolds.
we have a complete description of the motivic Gysin sequence for arbitrary symplectic bundles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a symplectic bundle over a smooth projective variety, the pushforward of MW-motives of the fiber is isomorphic to the pushforward of the MW-motives with the fiber removed.
we have constructed the MW-motivic version of the Gysin sequence.
we have a new approach to the study of the motive of $$HP^n$$ HP n and its application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show that, in a certain sense, the category of MW-motives is a natural setting to study motivic cohomology of quaternionic Grassmannians and of more general symplectic bundles.
we can compute MW-motives of some projective bundles in terms of the motive of the base and of the fibre.
the category of effective motives of a variety is not enough to compute its MW-motives.
